title: Incorrect totals
summary: Diagnose string concatenation and floating-point rounding in a receipt total.

scenario.briefing: Prices arrive from JSON as strings. The receipt shows 12.500.99 instead of 13.49, and small decimal amounts drift. Return an integer number of cents.

objectives.description: Convert string prices to numbers before arithmetic.
Return a stable integer cent total.

hints: The plus operator concatenates strings when one side is text.
Convert each price with Number before multiplying by 100.
Multiplying a decimal by 100 can still produce floating error. Round the final cents total.
Keep an integer totalCents, add Math.round(Number(price) * 100) for each price, and return it.

misconceptions.description: Adding prices without converting them to numbers.
misconceptions.feedback: When one operand is a string, + joins text. Convert prices to numbers before arithmetic.
Binary floating point cannot represent every decimal exactly. For money, work in integer cents or round a carefully computed cent value.

sections.title: Types decide operation meaning
sections.body: The + operator adds numbers but concatenates strings. Values from JSON, form fields, and URLs arrive as text. Converting to the intended type is part of validating input, not an optional detail.

sections.title: Money needs integer care
sections.body: Decimal fractions such as 0.1 cannot all be represented exactly in binary floating point. Storing and computing money in integer cents avoids most visible drift. If a computation must use decimals, round at a documented boundary.

vocabulary.definition: Changing a value from one type to another.
A binary representation of fractional numbers with limited precision.
Money stored as whole hundredths of a currency unit.

steps.title: Repair the receipt total
steps.prompt: Edit receipt.js. orderTotalCents(prices) receives string prices and returns an integer cent total. Run the tests.

steps.title: What does + do?
steps.prompt: What is the value of "2" + 3 in JavaScript?

quiz.explanation: One operand is a string, so + concatenates: "2" + 3 becomes "23".

hints: JavaScript converts the other side to text for +.
The result is the characters 2 and 3 together.

steps.title: Types and money

statements.label: External data must be converted and validated before arithmetic.
Integer cents avoid most decimal rounding drift.
Every decimal fraction is represented exactly in binary floating point.

steps.explanation: JavaScript performs implicit conversions, which can hide mistakes. Explicit conversion and integer cents make money calculations predictable.
